catalog.name: audit
catalog.summary: Failed jobs, stuck targets, publication inconsistencies across both pipelines, and stored dates that are not dates.
catalog.note: event counts cover the last 30 days, reported as `eventsSince`; consistency, delivery state and `storedDates` are current, not windowed. A non-empty `storedDates` means a column is holding a value every query will compare as text and no report will show as wrong: fix the writer, then the rows

catalog.name: video-library

catalog.note: The bot is where Maru attaches one at publishing time; this is the same store, for scripts that already exist somewhere else. catalog.note: reports the targets in scope; `apply` rewrites them

catalog.note: reports the targets in scope; `apply` replaces and republishes them

catalog.note: reports the targets in scope; `apply` republishes them

catalog.name: delete
catalog.summary: Take a publication down from the targets that support remote deletion.
catalog.note: reports the targets in scope; `apply` deletes them

catalog.name: purge
catalog.summary: Permanently remove an already-absent Studio publication and all of its stored state.
catalog.note: reports every row in scope; set `apply` only after the remote publication is gone

catalog.name: resume-from
catalog.summary: Point a half-published target at the post it should finish onto, then let the retry write the rest.
catalog.note: For a publication that goes out in more than one call and now names the wrong post, typically after a duplicate was removed by hand. The ordinary retry continues from whatever the job carries; this is how that is corrected. `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: draft-publish
catalog.summary: Send a draft that is already written to every platform it has enabled, now.
catalog.note: The `publish` command writes a new publication from text; this one publishes a draft that exists. `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: draft-schedule
catalog.summary: Put a draft in the queue for a time instead of publishing it now.
catalog.note: A bare wall clock is read in this Studio's time zone; an explicit offset is honoured as written. `reschedule` moves a publication that already has a plan. `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: draft-cancel
catalog.summary: Call off a draft and everything of it still waiting in the queue.
catalog.note: Nothing already delivered is touched; use `delete` for that. `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: video-publish
catalog.summary: Send a video draft to every platform it has chosen, now.

catalog.name: video-schedule
catalog.summary: Put every platform of a video draft in the queue for one time.
catalog.note: One time for all of them, because a per-platform time is a picker on the card. `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: video-cancel
catalog.summary: Call off a video: its queue, its reminders, and the YouTube upload it may already have made.
catalog.note: An upload YouTube already holds is kept private rather than deleted, and anything published needs removing by hand; the answer says which. `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: skip
catalog.summary: Finish a publication without a target that did not land, instead of retrying it.
catalog.note: The other answer to what `retry` asks, and the one the bot has always had next to it. Nothing is sent and nothing is removed from a platform: the jobs stop asking to be dealt with and the publication settles. Omit `target` to give up on every target that did not land; `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: resend
catalog.summary: Send an already-published post to a platform it never went to.
catalog.note: For a platform remembered after the fact, which `retry` cannot do: retry republishes what a target already delivered. A target that already has the post is refused, so this cannot publish it twice. `apply` performs it.
catalog.startHere: The post should have gone to one more platform.

catalog.name: settle
catalog.summary: Answer a target stuck in verification_required with what the platform actually shows.
catalog.note: Reconciliation resolves an ambiguous target by asking the platform about its stored id, so a worker lost before recording one leaves nothing to ask about. Name `external-id` to record the post as live, or omit it to report the post absent and queue it again; `apply` performs it.

catalog.name: video-retry
catalog.summary: Queue a failed video target again.
catalog.note: Only a target that failed, and a provider route is asked before it is repeated: the provider still holding a post id is queried under the fence that already covers that publication, and a new attempt is armed only if the answer is that the audience got nothing. That new attempt carries a new fence, so it can publish what the failed one never did. Answers with `settled` when the question alone resolved the target.

catalog.name: video-settle
catalog.summary: Answer a provider-delivered video target stuck awaiting verification.
catalog.note: Asks the provider what became of the publication and records the answer: a platform link means published, a provider-side failure sends the target back to `failed` where a retry can pick it up, anything else stays awaiting verification. Give `external_id`/`url` to record what you can see on the platform yourself, which outranks what the provider says. Provider routes only: a native upload has no idempotent replay to ask with.

catalog.name: refresh-site
catalog.summary: Re-render one locale's public page without touching social targets.

catalog.name: replace-media
catalog.summary: Swap the media of a published post on one target and re-render the site.
catalog.note: reports the target in scope; `apply` replaces it

catalog.name: reschedule
catalog.summary: Move a scheduled publication to another time.

catalog.name: publication-repair
catalog.summary: Reconcile publication rows against their jobs and targets.
catalog.note: scoped repair is preferred

catalog.name: disk
catalog.summary: What the data volume holds, and how much of it nothing points at.
catalog.note: Media caches are supposed to hold something -- they age out on a TTL. Story variants are not a cache: one whose source is gone is a file nothing will read or delete, and `orphaned` counts exactly those.
catalog.startHere: the data volume is filling up

catalog.name: media-reprocess
catalog.summary: Re-run media processing for one publication.

catalog.name: story-media-backfill
catalog.summary: Render the Story shapes missing from the media this Studio can still publish.
catalog.note: `missing_wanted` is the number to act on: a draft that publishes a Story points at that file, delivery only reads these files, so that publication will refuse. `missing_unused` is media no draft has asked a Story of -- normal, and left alone unless `all` is passed. Reports the plan; `apply` renders `limit` of them, one encode at a time -- a video is 8-12 seconds, so run it again until `remaining` is zero.
catalog.startHere: a Story is slow to publish, or refuses for want of prepared media

catalog.name: story-media-prune
catalog.summary: Remove Story variants whose source file is gone.
catalog.note: Retention takes a variant with its source, so this is for what accumulated before that and for files named by routes that no longer exist. A file a publish job's payload still names is reported under `held_by_a_publish_job` and never removed.

catalog.name: backup
catalog.summary: Copy the database to a timestamped file.

catalog.name: backup-stream
catalog.summary: Write one backup stream to stdout for a backup host to pull.
catalog.note: Nothing is written to this host: the stream is meant for `ssh <studio> ops backup-stream --what media > …` from the machine that keeps the backups. `doctor` fails once no media stream has been pulled for a week.

catalog.name: restore
catalog.summary: Replace the database with a backup.
catalog.note: replaces the database

catalog.name: format-record
catalog.summary: Record the message that proves a target carries a media format.

catalog.name: site-display-repair
catalog.summary: Restore editorial modification dates from a reviewed plan and remove site-only Story cards.
catalog.note: Without file, exports current content fingerprints and dates. A version-1 JSON plan restores only dates whose expected timestamp and editorial fingerprint still match. Removes generated Story cards from published site galleries; keeps their social delivery assets. Does not resend publications.

catalog.name: site-media-backfill
catalog.summary: Restore original proportions to published site galleries, newest posts first.
catalog.note: Replaces the old vertical viewer files using original uploads, including videos and thread attachments. Each locale switches after all its files exist. Missing uploads leave the current gallery intact. Does not resend social publications or delete historical URLs; repeat until remaining is zero.

catalog.name: site-responsive-backfill
catalog.summary: Create missing or outdated responsive images and video posters for published site media.
catalog.note: Reports the gap; apply writes the publication worker's WebP sizes, one source at a time. Does not change posts or re-encode video.

catalog.name: site-metadata
catalog.summary: Export published image metadata, or import reviewed alt descriptions and SEO titles.
catalog.note: Without file, exports published text hashes and images. With file, validates the version-1 JSON plan; apply saves it atomically and queues changed public URLs for IndexNow. Changed text and replaced images are protected. To correct existing copy, supply its exact expected_seo_title or expected_alt; stale edits fail. Does not resend publications.

catalog.name: site-media-deduplicate
catalog.summary: Collapse identical assets in media storage.

catalog.name: channel-connect
catalog.usage: channel-connect [--platform youtube|instagram] [--locale ru|en] [--provider native|zernio] [--target telegram|site_ru|site_en|threads_ru|threads_en|x|discord|telegram_stories|instagram_stories_ru|instagram_stories] [--account-id VALUE] [--label VALUE]
catalog.summary: Connect a publishing route.
catalog.note: A text or story route needs only `target`: it already names the platform and the language, and asking for them again is a way to store a channel that disagrees with itself. A video account needs `platform` with `locale`. An Instagram account connected for Reels does not carry the Story with it: connect `instagram_stories_ru` or `instagram_stories` when this Studio actually posts them, because a connected target is one the post screens offer and the queue waits for.

catalog.name: connect-link
catalog.summary: Start connecting an account, and say what has to happen next.
catalog.note: Open the signed, short-lived consent link. Threads and Instagram need their app id and secret, X its client id and secret, YouTube its client id and secret for that language, and all of them TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

catalog.name: channel-disable
catalog.summary: Disable a channel, keeping its publication history attributable.

catalog.name: credential-set
catalog.summary: Store an API key this Studio is handed rather than negotiates.
catalog.note: Reads the key from standard input, so it never appears in a command line or a shell history: `printf %s "$KEY" | ops credential-set --target zernio`. The key is checked against the service before it is stored, and .env is not consulted for it afterwards.

catalog.name: telegram-stories-login
catalog.summary: Sign this Studio's Stories account in and store its session.
catalog.note: Telegram Stories are posted by a user, not a bot, so the credential is an MTProto session. Needs TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_STORIES_API_ID, _API_HASH and _SESSION set first; run it with a terminal attached (docker compose exec -it) because it asks for the phone number, the code Telegram sends, and the 2FA password if the account has one.

catalog.name: threads-authorize
catalog.summary: Terminal fallback for obtaining a long-lived Threads token when the browser callback is unavailable.
catalog.note: The normal path is Studio → Channels. This fallback needs THREADS_APP_ID and THREADS_APP_SECRET, prints a link, then asks for the redirect address. Run it with a terminal attached (docker compose exec -it).

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.description: [delivery] Take a publication down from the targets that support remote deletion. (reports the targets in scope; `apply` deletes them)

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_resume_from
tools.description: [delivery] Point a half-published target at the post it should finish onto, then let the retry write the rest. apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_draft_schedule
tools.description: [delivery] Put a draft in the queue for a time instead of publishing it now. (A bare wall clock is read in this Studio's time zone; an explicit offset is honoured as written. `reschedule` moves a publication that already has a plan. `apply` performs it.)

at.description: when to publish, in this Studio's time zone unless it carries an offset

locale.description: which language to schedule; both by default

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_draft_cancel
tools.description: [delivery] Call off a draft and everything of it still waiting in the queue. (Nothing already delivered is touched; use `delete` for that. `apply` performs it.)

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_video_publish
tools.description: [delivery] Send a video draft to every platform it has chosen, now.

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_video_schedule
tools.description: [delivery] Put every platform of a video draft in the queue for one time. (One time for all of them, because a per-platform time is a picker on the card. `apply` performs it.)

at.description: when to publish, in this Studio's time zone unless it carries an offset

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_video_cancel
tools.description: [delivery] Call off a video: its queue, its reminders, and the YouTube upload it may already have made. (An upload YouTube already holds is kept private rather than deleted, and anything published needs removing by hand; the answer says which. `apply` performs it.)

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_skip
tools.description: [delivery] Finish a publication without a target that did not land, instead of retrying it. (The other answer to what `retry` asks, and the one the bot has always had next to it. Omit `target` to give up on every target that did not land; `apply` performs it.)

target.description: one target to give up on, or every unlanded one

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_resend
tools.description: [delivery] Send an already-published post to a platform it never went to. (For a platform remembered after the fact, which `retry` cannot do: retry republishes what a target already delivered. target.description: the target to send it to now

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_settle

(Reconciliation resolves an ambiguous target by asking the platform about its stored id, so a worker lost before recording one leaves nothing to ask about. apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_video_retry
tools.description: [delivery] Queue a failed video target again. (Only a target that failed, and a provider route is asked before it is repeated: the provider still holding a post id is queried under the fence that already covers that publication, and a new attempt is armed only if the answer is that the audience got nothing. tools.name: ops_video_settle
tools.description: [delivery] Answer a provider-delivered video target stuck awaiting verification. (Asks the provider what became of the publication and records the answer: a platform link means published, a provider-side failure sends the target back to `failed` where a retry can pick it up, anything else stays awaiting verification. external_id.description: what the platform shows, when you can see it

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.description: [delivery] Re-render one locale's public page without touching social targets.

target.description: accepted; a public page is not per target

apply.description: accepted; this repair always acts

tools.description: [delivery] Move a scheduled publication to another time.

at.description: in the configured timezone, or an ISO instant

tools.description: [delivery] Reconcile publication rows against their jobs and targets. (scoped repair is preferred)

ref.description: scope to one publication; omitted it sweeps everything

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_media_reprocess
tools.description: [media] Re-run media processing for one publication.

apply.description: perform the change; omitted it reports the plan only

tools.name: ops_channel_connect
tools.description: [channels] Connect a publishing route. (A text or story route needs only `target`: it already names the platform and the language, and asking for them again is a way to store a channel that disagrees with itself. A video account needs `platform` with `locale`. An Instagram account connected for Reels does not carry the Story with it: connect `instagram_stories_ru` or `instagram_stories` when this Studio actually posts them, because a connected target is one the post screens offer and the queue waits for.)

tools.name: ops_connect_link
tools.description: [channels] Start connecting an account, and say what has to happen next. (Open the signed, short-lived consent link. Threads and Instagram need their app id and secret, X its client id and secret, YouTube its client id and secret for that language, and all of them TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY.)

locale.description: which language's account, for platforms this Studio keeps two of

tools.description: [channels] Disable a channel, keeping its publication history attributable.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Record feedback or a bug report in this Studio's own journal, where its operator will see it. It is not sent anywhere.
